quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is a fast, spinning column of wind touching the ground!
quests.question: Tornado
quests.hint: This spinning wind can pick up light objects and carry them away.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Tornado is correct because it is a fast, spinning column of wind.
quests.funFact: A tornado's spinning winds can be some of the fastest winds on our whole planet!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is a light, gentle wind on a nice day!
quests.question: Breeze
quests.hint: This soft moving air might make a wind chime jingle softly.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Breeze is correct because it is a light, gentle wind.
quests.funFact: A gentle breeze is often just strong enough to make leaves flutter, but not fall!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is very light rain falling in tiny drops!
quests.question: Drizzle
quests.hint: This is much softer and lighter than a heavy rainstorm.
quests.explanation: That's right! Drizzle is correct because it is very light rain falling in tiny drops.
quests.funFact: Drizzle drops are so small and light that they can float gently on the breeze!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is a huge snowstorm with very strong, icy wind!
quests.question: Blizzard
quests.hint: This snowy storm can make it almost impossible to see outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Blizzard is correct because it is a huge snowstorm with strong, icy wind.
quests.funFact: During a big blizzard, snow can pile up higher than a front door!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a giant, slow-moving river made of solid ice!
quests.question: Glacier
quests.hint: This huge frozen giant moves so slowly you cannot even see it move.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Glacier is correct because it is a giant river of solid ice that moves slowly.
quests.funFact: Glaciers hold most of the fresh water on our entire planet!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a hard, curved covering found washed up on the beach!
quests.question: Shell
quests.hint: This hard little home once protected a small sea creature.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Shell is correct because it is a hard covering that washes up on the beach.
quests.funFact: You can sometimes hear a whooshing sound if you hold a big shell up to your ear!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a tall, hollow, fast-growing green plant!
quests.question: Bamboo
quests.hint: This plant can shoot up taller very quickly, almost overnight.
quests.explanation: That's right! Bamboo is correct because it is a tall, hollow plant that grows extremely fast.
quests.funFact: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that streaks brightly across the night sky for just a second!
quests.question: Shooting Star
quests.hint: Some people make a wish the moment they spot this quick flash of light.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Shooting Star is correct because it streaks brightly across the sky for a moment.
quests.funFact: A shooting star isn't really a star at all — it's a tiny piece of space rock!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that fills the night sky with glowing waves of color!
quests.question: Aurora
quests.hint: This colorful glow is best seen in places very far up north.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Aurora is correct because it fills the night sky with glowing waves of color.
quests.funFact: An aurora can glow green, pink, or even purple across the night sky!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is spinning water pulling everything toward its center!
quests.question: Whirlpool
quests.hint: This spinning circle of water forms where two ocean currents meet.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Whirlpool is correct because it is spinning water pulling toward its center.
quests.funFact: Some ocean whirlpools are strong enough to be seen from an airplane!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that shoots hot water high into the air from underground!
quests.question: Geyser
quests.hint: Deep underground, super-hot water builds up until it bursts out like a fountain.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Geyser is correct because it shoots hot water high into the air from underground.
quests.funFact: One famous geyser, called Old Faithful, shoots water into the air like clockwork!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where a huge pile of snow suddenly slides down a mountain!
quests.question: Avalanche
quests.hint: This can happen quickly on a steep, snowy mountainside.
quests.explanation: Great job! An Avalanche is correct because it is snow sliding suddenly down a mountain.
quests.funFact: A small sound or movement can sometimes be enough to start a big snow slide!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a thin, sparkly layer of ice on cold mornings!
quests.question: Frost
quests.hint: You might see this sparkly coating on grass or car windows early in the morning.
quests.explanation: Yes! Frost is correct because it is a thin, sparkly layer of ice that forms on cold mornings.
quests.funFact: Frost forms when tiny water droplets in the air freeze straight onto a cold surface!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where the ocean's water slowly rises and falls each day!
quests.question: Tide
quests.hint: This slow rise and fall is caused by the pull of the Moon.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Tide is correct because it is the ocean water slowly rising and falling each day.
quests.funFact: The Moon's pull is the main reason the ocean has tides at all!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a long, pointy piece of ice hanging down!
quests.question: Icicle
quests.hint: This often hangs from a roof or a branch after it starts to melt and refreeze.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Icicle is correct because it is a long, pointy piece of hanging ice.
quests.funFact: Icicles form drop by drop as dripping water freezes again in the cold air!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that forms a funnel shape reaching down from a storm cloud!
quests.question: Tornado
quests.hint: People go to a safe, low room inside when they see this coming.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Tornado is correct because it forms a spinning funnel shape from a storm cloud.
quests.funFact: Tornadoes usually only last for a few minutes, even though they are so powerful!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that feels cool and soft against your skin on a warm day!
quests.question: Breeze
quests.hint: Sailors love this gentle push of moving air on a calm sunny day.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Breeze is correct because it is a soft, cool movement of air.
quests.funFact: Ocean breezes happen because the sea and the land warm up at different speeds!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where the sky sprinkles just a little bit of rain!
quests.question: Drizzle
quests.hint: You might not even need an umbrella for this gentle, light rain.
quests.explanation: Well done! Drizzle is correct because it is only a light sprinkle of rain.
quests.funFact: Drizzle often falls from low, grey clouds instead of tall stormy ones!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that fills the air with blowing snow and freezing wind!
quests.question: Blizzard
quests.hint: Schools sometimes close for the day because of this icy, snowy storm.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Blizzard is correct because it fills the air with blowing snow and freezing wind.
quests.funFact: Some blizzards can last for several days without stopping!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a massive block of ice covering land for miles!
quests.question: Glacier
quests.hint: This icy giant can be older than almost anything else on Earth.
quests.explanation: Well done! A Glacier is correct because it is a massive, ancient block of ice covering land.
quests.funFact: Some glaciers are thousands and thousands of years old!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that comes in many swirly shapes and colors along the shore!
quests.question: Shell
quests.hint: Kids love collecting these in a bucket during a beach visit.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Shell is correct because it comes in many swirly shapes and colors on the shore.
quests.funFact: Some sea shells can be over one hundred years old!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object with a tall, jointed stem that grows in thick green groves!
quests.question: Bamboo
quests.hint: This plant is actually a giant type of grass, not a tree.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bamboo is correct because its tall, jointed stems grow in thick green groves.
quests.funFact: Bamboo is actually a giant grass, even though it grows as tall as a tree!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that leaves a bright, glowing trail as it falls through the sky!
quests.question: Shooting Star
quests.hint: You have to look up quickly, because this flash disappears in an instant.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Shooting Star is correct because it leaves a glowing trail as it streaks through the sky.
quests.funFact: On a clear night, you might see several shooting stars in just one hour!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that makes the sky ripple with color near the North Pole!
quests.question: Aurora
quests.hint: People often travel a long way just to see this glowing night sky show.
quests.explanation: Well done! An Aurora is correct because it makes the sky ripple with color near the poles.
quests.funFact: Auroras happen when tiny particles from the Sun bump into our sky high above the Earth!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that looks like a swirling circle in a river or the sea!
quests.question: Whirlpool
quests.hint: This swirling water spins round and round in the very same spot.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Whirlpool is correct because it is water that swirls round and round in one spot.
quests.funFact: Small whirlpools can even form in your bathtub when the water drains out!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that erupts like a fountain of steaming hot water!
quests.question: Geyser
quests.hint: This natural fountain gets its heat from deep inside the Earth.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Geyser is correct because it erupts like a fountain of hot, steaming water.
quests.funFact: There are only a few places on Earth where geysers are found!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that sends snow rushing down a steep, snowy slope!
quests.question: Avalanche
quests.hint: Skiers and climbers must be very careful of this on tall, snowy mountains.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Avalanche is correct because it sends snow rushing down a steep slope.
quests.funFact: Avalanches can move down a mountain faster than a car drives on the highway!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that draws icy, feather-like patterns on a cold window!
quests.question: Frost
quests.hint: This thin ice forms overnight when the air gets cold enough.
quests.explanation: That's right! Frost is correct because it forms icy, feather-like patterns on cold surfaces.
quests.funFact: Every frost pattern that forms on a window is completely one of a kind!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that uncovers more sandy beach when it goes out!
quests.question: Tide
quests.hint: At certain times of day, the water moves back and shows more of the sand.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Tide is correct because the water moves back and uncovers more of the beach.
quests.funFact: Some beaches show a much bigger stretch of sand during low tide than high tide!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that looks like a frozen, dripping candle hanging from a branch!
quests.question: Icicle
quests.hint: Sunlight can make this clear, icy shape sparkle and glisten.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Icicle is correct because it looks like a frozen drip of ice hanging from a branch.
quests.funFact: The longest icicles ever recorded were taller than a house!
